questions.text: The angle of ___ is equal to the angle of ___.

questions.prompt: A ray hits a mirror with an angle of incidence of 35°. What is the angle of reflection?
questions.explain: The angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence.

questions.prompt: A ray makes an angle of 50° with the MIRROR SURFACE. What is the angle of reflection?
questions.hint: Angles are measured from the normal, which is at 90° to the mirror.
questions.explain: Angle of incidence = 90° − 50° = 40°, so the angle of reflection = 40°.

options: at 90° to the mirror at the point where the ray hits
questions.explain: The normal is perpendicular to the surface at the point of incidence.
Smooth surfaces give regular reflection; rough surfaces scatter light.

questions.prompt: Why can everyone in a classroom read the whiteboard, but a mirror only shows you certain things?
options: The whiteboard's rough surface scatters light in all directions (diffuse reflection)
The whiteboard makes its own light
questions.explain: Diffuse reflection sends light everywhere, so everyone can see the board.

questions.prompt: You have a plane mirror, a ray box, a protractor and paper. Describe how you would test the law of reflection.
questions.modelAnswer: Place the mirror upright on paper and draw a line along it. Draw the normal at 90° to the mirror. Shine a ray from the ray box at the mirror where the normal meets it, at an angle of incidence of 20°. Mark the reflected ray with two dots and measure the angle of reflection from the normal with the protractor. Repeat for 30°, 40°, 50° and 60°. Record the results in a table and check whether ∠i = ∠r each time.
rubric: Vary the angle of incidence over several values
Measure the angle of reflection from the normal
Record in a table and compare
questions.explain: Criterion B: a method that would give reliable data.

questions.prompt: Adam's results: ∠i = 20°, 40°, 60°; ∠r = 21°, 39°, 60°. What is the best conclusion?
options: The law of reflection is wrong
∠i and ∠r are equal within measurement error
questions.explain: Small differences of about 1° come from measuring errors; the pattern supports ∠i = ∠r.
